title: Canonicalize embeddings/rerank paging and status matrix with adapter shim
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Multiple clients rely on legacy embeddings/rerank endpoints that diverge in cursor semantics, page size behavior, and HTTP error shapes. This creates operational confusion (client retries, double-charging token meters, and unclear backoff guidance) and blocks downstream SDKs from providing a single migration surface. Goal: Ship a compatibility layer (adapter shim) that normalizes legacy and new clients into a single canonical contract for paging and errors, plus a migration playbook for customers. Constraints: Must not change token accounting, must be opt-in behind a compatibility flag for the first rollout, and must be reversible via feature toggle. Must work for hosted API and Dedicated routing.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter shim translates legacy cursor formats (legacy-cursor-v1) into canonical opaque cursor and back for responses within the same request window
HTTP error mapping documented and implemented: transient (429/503) vs permanent (400/403/422) with recommended Retry-After semantics
Page_size stability: server enforces max_page_size=100 and returns explicit page_size_used in responses for billing reconciliation
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) release adapters that interoperate with both legacy and canonical responses without behavioral regressions
End-to-end test suite with 12 canonical vectors covering cursor expiry, partial pages, empty-result pages, and error propagation
Rollout plan with 5% canary, metrics dashboard, and automatic rollback on regression signals within 24h
migration_playbook: Step 0: Notify customers in affected bucket and open migration opt-in form
Step 1: Enable compatibility flag for a small subset of clients (5%) and run canary for 72h
Step 2: Collect metrics: error-rate, request-latency-95th, token-accounting-delta, customer-reported-failures
Step 3: Ship SDK patch that decodes legacy cursors and exposes canonical_cursor on response objects
Step 4: Gradually increase rollout to 50% over 7 days while monitoring rollback signals
Step 5: Announce deprecation timeline for legacy-only behavior and provide sample migration snippets
Step 6: When stable at 95% rollout, flip default compatibility flag and start sunsetting legacy contract after 90 days
implementation_notes: Adapter shim will live in api-gateway layer to intercept /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank requests
Cursor strategy: canonical cursor is base64(JSON) containing {v, model, offset, ttl} signed with HMAC; adapter will accept legacy tokens and emit canonical ones
Error mapping: map legacy 429 burst -> 429 with Retry-After header; throttle signals map to 503 when infra constrained; include machine-readable error.code and error.subcode
Pagination: server returns {items, next_cursor, page_size_used, total_known} where total_known is optional for search-backed datasets
Telemetry: emit compat.adapter.enabled, compat.adapter.errors, compat.adapter.duration_ms, compat.cursor.conv_failures
SDK impacts: add decode_legacy_cursor(), expose response.page_size_used, and a migration flag in client config
Billing: billing team will reconcile based on page_size_used to avoid double-counting tokens during adapter translation
rollback_plan: Immediate: toggle compatibility flag off for affected region via control plane
Short-term: route traffic back to legacy handler and mark change in incident log
Post-mortem: freeze rollout, revert SDKs if needed, and schedule emergency patch for next release
